note: What this model asserts about the OBC1 and where each assertion comes from. One cartridge carried this chip and no manufacturer document for it is known to exist, so most of what is here rests on a reference implementation. One thing does not, and it is the most interesting entry in the file.

order: a manufacturer document for the OBC1, of which there is none
Nintendo's documented OAM structure, for anything the chip's layout mirrors
the reference implementation, for everything else
authority.why: This chip exists to feed OAM. It holds sprite attributes and hands the console a moving window onto them, so the shape of what it holds is the shape of what OAM expects, and OAM is documented. Where the two line up, Nintendo's figure is evidence about this chip even though Nintendo never described this chip.
authority.whatIsMissing: Any document naming this part. Searched on 2026-08-21; nothing was found, and the chip appears in a single cartridge.

comparedAgainst.what: An independent implementation, built from a pinned commit, asked every address the chip answers.

developmentManual.title: SNES Development Manual, Book 1
developmentManual.note: Read here for one table. The packed offset this record carries follows from the object attribute table's structure, read off page A-3 of this copy. snes-graphics-python pinned the same file first. The pin is repeated rather than referred to so a reader holding a different scan can tell before they start.

documentsNote: One entry, read here for the one table the packed offset rests on. No manufacturer document for this chip is known to exist: everything else in this record comes from the reference implementation and from the one cartridge that carries the part, which are rungs below the top of the ladder and are labelled as such.

packedOffset.why: The offset from a base address to the packed two-bit attributes. It is exactly the size of the OAM low table, which Nintendo documents as 128 sprites of four bytes each. The chip lays its memory out the way OAM is laid out, so this figure comes from a document rather than from a reimplementation.
packedOffset.source: The OBJECT DATA table on page A-3 of Nintendo's SNES Development Manual, Book 1
packedOffset.quote: OBJECT DATA. OAM ADDRESS (Decimal), D15 to D0. 000 and 001: OBJ 0. 002 and 003: OBJ 1. 252 and 253: OBJ 126. 254 and 255: OBJ 127. 256: OBJ 7 - OBJ 0. 257: OBJ 15 - OBJ 8. 270: OBJ 119 - OBJ 112. 271: OBJ 127 - OBJ 120.
packedOffset.howItWasRead: The table is a figure. The scan's text layer carries its heading and scatters its cells, so the rows were read off the rendered page. Each OAM address is one word, D15 to D0, so OBJ 0 to OBJ 127 take words 0 to 255, four bytes each, and the table of two bits per sprite starts at word 256, which is byte 512.

windowStart.why: Where the chip's window begins in the cartridge's address space.
windowStart.evidence: The reference implementation, corroborated by the driver in the one cartridge that carries this chip.
windowStart.howToSettleIt: A cartridge board schematic, or a continuity reading.

windowEnd.howToSettleIt: A cartridge board schematic, or a continuity reading.

ramBytes.why: How much memory the chip holds, which is the width of its window.
ramBytes.evidence: The reference implementation, and the window it answers across.
ramBytes.howToSettleIt: A die photograph, or a package marking naming the memory.

baseAddresses.why: The two places the window can point at, selected by one bit of a register.
baseAddresses.evidence: The reference implementation. The two are 0x400 apart, which is twice the size of an OAM low table, so each base has room for a table and its packed attributes.
baseAddresses.howToSettleIt: A die photograph of the address decode.

registers.why: The seven addresses that do not behave like memory.
registers.evidence: Two readings that do not share a source. The reference implementation, and the driver routine in both releases of the one cartridge, walked without running it: six of the seven addresses are ones that code reaches, and the two releases agree. The seventh, 0x7FF4, is not reached by an instruction carrying its whole address, which is all a walk can see.
registers.howToSettleIt: A die photograph, or a disassembly of that driver read independently.

unwrittenByte.why: What memory holds before anything is written, which the reset restores.
unwrittenByte.howToSettleIt: A measurement of a real cartridge immediately after power on.

notStated: Every register address. No manufacturer document names this part at all, so nothing here is a quote.
What the chip does with an address inside its window that is neither memory nor one of the seven registers, beyond what the reference does.
Anything about timing. How long the chip takes to answer, and whether the console can outrun it, is unmodelled and unmeasured.
Whether the two base addresses are the only two, or the only two that cartridge used.
